question: A 34-year-old man presents with multiple painful ulcers on his penis. He says that the ulcers all appeared suddenly at the same time 3 days ago. He reports that he is sexually active with multiple partners and uses condoms inconsistently. He is afebrile and his vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination reveals multiple small shallow ulcers with an erythematous base and without discharge. There is significant inguinal lymphadenopathy present. Which of the following is the most likely etiologic agent of this patient’s ulcers?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Multiple painful ulcers on the penis" -> "Sudden appearance of ulcers" -> "Consistent with a viral infection" -> "Inguinal lymphadenopathy present" -> "Herpes simplex virus is a common cause" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Multiple painful ulcers on the penis" -> "Ulcers with an erythematous base" -> "No discharge present" -> "Inguinal lymphadenopathy suggests an infectious etiology" -> "Herpes simplex virus is likely" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Patient is sexually active with multiple partners" -> "Inconsistent condom use increases risk of STIs" -> "Sudden onset of ulcers" -> "Herpes simplex virus commonly presents this way" -> "Other options less likely due to presentation" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Multiple shallow ulcers on the penis" -> "Significant inguinal lymphadenopathy" -> "Herpes simplex virus can cause this presentation" -> "Other STIs typically have different characteristics" -> 75%
analysis: The patient's presentation of multiple painful ulcers on the penis, which appeared suddenly, along with significant inguinal lymphadenopathy, is highly suggestive of genital herpes, which is caused by the herpes simplex virus (HSV). The ulcers are shallow with an erythematous base, consistent with herpes lesions. Other options like Chlamydia trachomatis and Treponema pallidum (syphilis) typically present differently, and Haemophilus ducreyi (causing chancroid) usually presents with more pronounced purulent discharge. Therefore, the most likely etiologic agent is herpes simplex virus.
